claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi is a single-phase FCC alloy.
Equiatomic FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Previously examined FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
The proposed intervention is to introduce about 10 at.% Al while targeting Fe30Co30Ni30Al10.
Fe30Co30Ni30Al10 preserves a near-equiatomic composition and high configurational entropy.
Suitable rapid solidification or annealing can retain Fe30Co30Ni30Al10 as a single-phase FCC alloy.
Al substitution produces localized lattice distortions in the modified alloy.
Al is sufficiently size-mismatched relative to Ni to create local lattice strain.
The Al-induced strain enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Al substitution creates additional magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
Enhanced anisotropy and domain-wall pinning increase the energy barrier for domain reversal and therefore increase coercivity.
Compositional substitution can substantially increase coercivity in an Al-Co-Fe-Ni-based high-entropy-alloy family.
Fe30Co30Ni30Al10 will have at least 50% greater coercivity than equiatomic FeCoNi.
Fe30Co30Ni30Al10 will have greater coercivity than the prior FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The coercivity increase will occur without significantly compromising saturation magnetization.
Composition and annealing conditions can alter phase stability and cause phase decomposition in Al-Co-Fe-Ni-based alloys.
Phase segregation or departure from the stipulated entropy range could preclude the proposed coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: Replacing 10 percentage points of Ni in equiatomic FeCoNi would nominally yield approximately Fe33.3Co33.3Ni23.3Al10, not Fe30Co30Ni30Al10; the stated target instead dilutes Fe, Co, and Ni together.

The target Fe30Co30Ni30Al10 is described as near-equiatomic even though Al is present at one-third the concentration of each other element, creating tension with the stated requirement to preserve a near-equiatomic composition.
